access_classes.means: Served the content to an anonymous browser.

Subscription press we hold no licence for. Either it served a subscription or registration wall instead of the content, or (for a publisher marked paywall in its page.json) it refused the anonymous browser with 401 or 403 before any wall. Counted apart from bot-challenge since 22 October 2026.
Served a bot or browser challenge (Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, Vercel). The challenge page's hash is kept as the record.
Wants a signed-in account (some social posts).
Refused because of where the request came from.
404 or 410: the page no longer exists at this address.
5xx, a timeout, a DNS failure or a refused connection: the site is not answering. For the affected sites this is the finding.
Listed, but the watcher is told not to fetch it (licence or editorial decision).

tips.says: Their browser extension, php2shell-checker, was just approved on the Chrome Web Store. It checks whether a website runs outdated PHP or a supported PHP application such as WordPress. They describe it as privacy friendly and read-only, with nothing leaving the browser, and aimed at CISOs in the SME segment as easier than running scripts.
to_check: The publisher named on the store listing, and whether it matches who made the claim
The permissions the listing and the manifest ask for, against 'read-only, nothing leaves the browser'
The version history and user count, run by run
Whether it detects the fixed versions (8.5.12 and the backports) correctly

tips.received: 2026-10-26, about 18:30 UTC (the screenshot's phone clock reads 21:28 local time)
tips.says: A brief update on the critical vulnerabilities in PHP. 'We have not yet validated exploitation in the wild and we have no evidence of successful wide scale exploitation.' Several exploit PoCs are circulating, many 'vibe-coded' and incapable of remote code execution; some validated PoCs are capable of RCE against default deployments of mod_php but not PHP-FPM. 'Nonetheless, exploitation may have already begun in a limited fashion.' Advice: patch and restart on PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35; layer WAF or proxy safeguards and server configuration if patching must wait; monitor abnormal session traffic and rotate keys and passwords on internet-facing PHP systems exposed before patching. They say their Cloud Security blog post is being updated continually. At the screenshot: 501 reactions, 31 comments, 88 reposts.
to_check: The post's link, for its exact time and its text as posted (a LinkedIn page cannot be captured: it is a login wall)
The Google Cloud Security blog post the author says he is updating: its address, its update times and what it says on exploitation
Whether 'validated PoCs capable of RCE against default mod_php, not PHP-FPM' matches PHP's own statement (PHP's advisory rates mod_php highest and says it demonstrated an exploit there)

Whether the OX Security article can be read (the watch's capture is a bot-challenge page) and what figures it gives for patching, against the Censys count of 1.57 million of about 2.6 million hosts unpatched on 21 October

Whether 'no evidence of successful wide scale exploitation' agrees with the others in the ledger record is-it-exploited (Amazon says 'broadly exploited'; CISA and officials in Germany, the Netherlands and Japan have seen none succeed; Cloudflare says it observed attack traffic)
